title: Repeating key word of 1-13 plus a steady step (per letter or once per pass, every start phase) on one hidden alphabet: both sides hidden (Vigenere, Beaufort) or one side hidden against A-Z / KRYPTOS, solved exactly mod 13 and mod 2 with distinct places required
k4_result: 15,450 settings (6 layouts x p 1-13 x s 1-25 x letter form and pass form at every phase; in V and B the steps s = 1, 2, 13 stand for all 25 by unit scaling). Decided part, 13,221 settings: 0 fits that read as English. Half-hidden layouts at p 1-9 (hp: 11 down to 4-5 loop tests; hc: 10 down to 3): 0 settings pass the loops (chance expects about 0.01). V and B at p 1 (3 tests): 0 pass. V at p 2-7 and 9, B at p 2-10: loops pass where they exist (0-2 tests) but NO placing puts the clue letters on different places, exact search, 0 settings with a fit. Fits that were listed in full and completed on the big model (V p 8: 216 settings; hpAZ p 13: 90; hcKR p 12: 26; 332 settings in all): best reading -6.04 (hcKR p 12, s 12 per letter: KWMYITASQUEGSGRAPACFM...), English needs -5.1. Undecided, 2,229 settings: V p 10-13, B p 11-13 (0 loop tests, fits in almost every setting, too many to list) and hcAZ / hcKR p 13 (39 and 26 settings with too many fits).
controls: 20 shuffled K4s, same search. Best completed readings -6.00 to -6.63 (K4 -6.04, inside the spread). Fully listed fit settings per shuffle 104-634 (K4 332); cells with undecided settings per shuffle 8-19 (K4 9). Shuffles often have K4's loop-test counts in the half-hidden hp layouts (20/20) but rarely in hc (0-2/20 at p 1-9) and V/B at short words (3-6/20). K4 is blocked MORE than a typical shuffle by the different-places rule: shuffles have fits at V p 7-9 (mean 26-84 settings) and B p 6-10 (mean 4-198), K4 has 0.
planted: 5/5 in decided cells read back as the best reading of the whole cell (all s, forms, phases): V word 7 step 3 per pass (97/97, -4.42), hcKR word 5 step 2 per pass (97/97, -4.42), hpKR word 5 step 2 per pass (92/97, -4.59), V word 1 step 7 (97/97, -4.82), hpAZ word 9 step 4 per letter (97/97, -4.34). The idea's second plant, Beaufort word 11 step 1 per letter, lies in an undecided cell (0 loop tests): its true setting survives the exact test, but it was not read back (two hill-climbs over the fit space and over the whole alphabet both failed on it).
scope_limits: Undecided and NOT ruled out: one hidden alphabet on both sides with a word of 10-13 (Vigenere) or 11-13 (Beaufort) plus any step; half-hidden with a word of 13 against A-Z/KRYPTOS on the cipher side (65 settings). In those cells the clues leave 0 loop tests and millions of placings, so only a working English solver could decide. Not covered at all: words over 13, steps that change, a step added at other intervals than every letter or every pass, two different hidden alphabets, a transposition layer.

negative.family: Stepped repeating key on a hidden alphabet
negative.hypothesis: K4 uses one hidden tableau alphabet with key k_i = w[i mod p] + s*i or w[i mod p] + s*floor((i+phase)/p) (a key word moved on by a constant step), p 1-13.
negative.scope: p 1-13, s 1-25, letter and pass form (every phase), layouts: one hidden alphabet on both sides (Vigenere and Beaufort form), hidden plain side against A-Z or KRYPTOS, hidden cipher side against A-Z or KRYPTOS. Exact solve of the 24 clue equations mod 13 and mod 2 in the 26 places and p word values, then exact backtracking for a placing with all clue letters on different places; fits listed in full (<=40 per setting, <=3000 with 3+ loop tests) were completed on the big English model.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope for hidden plain side p 1-13, hidden cipher side p 1-12, both sides hidden V p 1-9 and B p 1-10: 0 loop passes where 3+ tests exist, 0 distinct placings in V p 2-7, 9 and B p 2-10, and the 332 fully listed fit settings read at best -6.04 against -5.1 needed (controls: 20 shuffled K4s, best -6.00 to -6.63; planted 5/5 in decided cells). Undecided: V p 10-13, B p 11-13, hcAZ/hcKR p 13.

follow_ups: A real English solver for the undecided cells (one hidden alphabet, word of 10-13 plus a step): the fit space is an affine lattice of dimension 5-9 mod 13 with most points putting two letters on one place; neither coordinate annealing nor annealing on the whole alphabet with the clues as penalties found a planted Beaufort word-11 text. Something like a branch-and-bound over the lattice that scores partially decrypted columns may work.

K4's clue letters forbid distinct placings at Vigenere word lengths 2-7 and 9 and Beaufort 2-10 for EVERY step, more often than shuffled K4s do: the same distinct-places test can be run cheaply on any other key family with a free word plus a known term.
